script.text: Good morning! I'm Kelly, and this is your daily lesson for May 15. Today we're exploring two powerful ideas together.
You and a butterfly share an ancestor.  So do you and a fish, a worm, a sponge.  Every animal on Earth—from elephants to insects—traces back to a common origin.

All life uses the same genetic code—DNA with the same four letters, the same way of encoding proteins. This shared language strongly suggests all life descended from one original organism. Different species, same underlying programming. Compare DNA and you find surprising similarities.  Humans and chimps share 98.
Today's wisdom: Here's today's wisdom: Diversity arises from unity.  All animal variety—millions of species—branched from common origins.
Now let's take what we learned and put it into practice.
Today's growth challenge is Family Recognition - See the Connection.

Here's your activity: Next time you see an animal—any animal—remember you share ancestors. How many generations back? Millions. But the connection is real. Does knowing this change how you see that bird, that dog, that insect? This helps you feel connection to other animals.
And here's how today's lessons connect: What you learned about how animals are related can be applied to family recognition - see the connection. Practice makes progress.
That's today's lesson. Learn something, grow a little. I'll see you tomorrow with something new. Stay curious!
